How to convert a Word document to PDF

Open Word or Excel to PDF, add the .docx or .xlsx file and press Make the PDF.

Word or Excel to PDF →Free. Nothing is uploaded.

How to do it

  1. Open Word or Excel to PDF.
  2. Add the .docx or .xlsx files.
  3. Press Make the PDF.
  4. Save the PDF, or tap Then to merge or compress it.

What is kept

Headings, lists, tables, links and pictures are laid out on A4, with the words kept as real text you can select and search. Wide spreadsheets go on sideways pages. Malayalam, Hindi and other scripts are drawn by your browser, so they show correctly.

What is not, yet

Fonts become the nearest of Helvetica, Times or Courier. Headers, footers and footnotes are left out for now. Older .doc and .xls files need saving as .docx or .xlsx first.

If you have Word, Google Docs or LibreOffice, their own Save as PDF or Download as PDF keeps your exact fonts and headers. This tool is for when you do not have them, such as on a phone, or on a work computer where you should not upload files.

After converting

Join it with other PDFs using Merge, or bring it under an upload limit with Compress. Going the other way is PDF to Word.

Questions people ask

Is my document uploaded?

No. The PDF is laid out in your browser.

Can I convert an Excel sheet?

Yes. Each sheet comes out as a table; wide ones on sideways pages.

Why does my .doc file not work?

Only the newer .docx and .xlsx are read. Open the old file in an office app and save it as .docx first.

Can I convert several files at once?

Yes. Add them all; each becomes its own PDF, and Merge can join them afterwards.

Your file stays on your device. Foolscap does the work inside your browser, so nothing is uploaded and there is nothing for anyone to keep. How you can check
